subject: Tenor tether, billing cadence, and amendment approach
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@greenbridge.co>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Tenor tether, billing cadence, and amendment approach

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a short proposal for how we can reshape the upcoming renewal to match GreenBridge's fiscal alignment while keeping capacity predictable as you ramp into H1. Attached is a PDF with the high-level numbers (GreenBridge_MA_Pricing_v3.pdf).

Proposal summary (high-level):
- Term: move from month-to-month/annual to an 18-month hybrid tenor that co-terms to your Mar 31 fiscal boundary.
- Ramp: staircase ramp (30% year 1, 70% year 2 on committed throughput) to reduce up-front exposure.
- Billing cadence: quarter-by-quarter invoicing to help your cash flow / budgeting.
- Auto-renew: enabled by default but with a 60-day opt-out window before co-term anniversary.
- Early payment: 2% credit if year invoice paid within 15 days.

As discussed, we can layer a small credit buffer at kickoff to offset the first-quarter overspend risk while you onboard traffic.

Can you confirm that co-terming to Mar 31 and quarterly billing are acceptable in principle? If yes, I’ll loop in Legal to draft a short amendment and share a redline for your procurement team.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachment: GreenBridge_MA_Pricing_v3.pdf (1 page, pricing summary)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@greenbridge.co>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenbridge.co, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@greenbridge.co>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tenor tether, billing cadence, and amendment approach

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifying questions from my side and our finance lead:

1) Co-term to Mar 31 — do you mean the 18-month term would end on Mar 31 of the second calendar year (i.e., align with our FY)? We prefer alignment to our FY end, not a rolling 18-month anniversary.
2) Quarterly invoices are fine, but our procurement prefers invoices to be aligned to quarter boundaries and not mid-quarter billing. Can you confirm we can align invoicing to calendar quarter cutoffs?
3) Auto-renew: we generally accept auto-renew but need an opt-out window that is longer than 30 days; 60 days sounds reasonable and we'll confirm with Legal.

Also, please include a brief note on what happens if usage materially overshoots committed throughput in Q1 (we need a clear overage policy and a runway before we step to higher capacity).

Procurement copied for routing — they will want the amendment and a redline.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product Operations, GreenBridge Analytics
alyssa@greenbridge.co

---
Reply inline below:
> As discussed, we can layer a small credit buffer at kickoff to offset the first-quarter overspend risk while you onboard traffic.

That would help. If you can quantify the buffer (one month of committed tokens as credit?) that will speed approvals.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Tenor tether, billing cadence, and amendment approach (internal)

Jordan / Kim —

Quick internal note before we respond to Alyssa: I ran scenarios against the current pricing model (see attached pricing_model_notes.xlsx). Two practical options to present:

Option A (conservative): 18-month co-term to Mar 31 (ends at FY boundary) with quarterly billing aligned to quarter cutoffs. Provide 1 month of committed capacity as a kickoff credit and a 90-day grace for overage throttling before stepping up to a higher commit band. No discount to list price beyond the credit.

Option B (growth-friendly): 24-month term with a front-loaded credit equal to 1.5 months, staircase ramp of 25/75, and a 6-month lookback true-up at the end of the first year. Slightly lower unit price (3% off list) in exchange for longer commitment.

I lean A for speed — procurement gets comfortable faster and finance doesn't have to model a longer sail. But if we want to lock bigger ARR we can push B. Kimberly — can you validate the cash impact of A vs B if we give the 1 month credit? I sketched the numbers in the sheet.

Ben Carter
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: pricing_model_notes.xlsx (calc tabs: optionA / optionB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@greenbridge.co>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tenor tether, billing cadence, and amendment approach

Alyssa —

Thanks — below is a concrete path that addresses your asks and keeps procurement details tidy. I’ve attached a short draft amendment for review (Draft_Amendment_4821.pdf).

What we propose (final recommendation):
- Term & co-term: 18-month effective term that explicitly co-terms to Mar 31 FY boundary (meaning the term will be sized so the contract anniversary is Mar 31 at the end of the 18 months).
- Billing cadence: invoicing on calendar quarter boundaries (we’ll prorate the initial partial quarter to match your next quarter cutoff).
- Ramp & overage: staircase ramp 30% / 70% of committed throughput. If usage exceeds committed throughput, we allow a 90-day operational runway (overage accrues as post-paid tokens billed at overage rate, but we will not force an immediate commit jump during that 90-day runway unless both sides agree).
- Kickoff credit: 1 month of committed capacity provided as an invoice credit to offset onboarding variance.
- Auto-renew: contract auto-renews but GreenBridge may opt out with 60 days notice prior to co-term anniversary.
- Pricing: keep list unit price, apply the kickoff credit; Ben has an alternate 24-month option if you prefer a deeper unit discount — we can surface that in a separate doc.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: we’ll send a redline and the draft amendment into DocuSign once you confirm the above in principle.
2) Legal review: Jordan will CC Legal on the redline if you want us to expedite (we can route to our contracts team SLA).
3) Finance: Kimberly will confirm the invoice proration approach and the credit mechanics.

If that all looks good I’ll generate a DocuSign link and include a short SOW addendum with the committed throughput table.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick call if procurement wants to walk the changes.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
Attachment: Draft_Amendment_4821.pdf (3 pages, draft amendment + committable throughput table)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@greenbridge.co>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenbridge.co, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@greenbridge.co>
Date: 2026-12-05T17:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tenor tether, billing cadence, and amendment approach

Jordan —

This looks good in principle. Procurement will run the amendment through Legal and routing; Rajiv has flagged no major concerns on the surface. Please:

- Send a redline against our standard MSA (procurement prefers a redline rather than a fresh doc).
- Include the SOW table with committed throughput by quarter and the exact language for the 90-day overage runway.
- Generate the DocuSign link and we’ll route to our PO process once Legal signs off.

We’re comfortable with the 1 month kickoff credit and quarterly invoices aligned to quarter boundaries. Thanks for being flexible on the opt-out window and the overage runway.

We can finalize after Legal redline; feel free to attach the redline to the DocuSign envelope so procurement can see both in one place.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Product Operations, GreenBridge Analytics
alyssa@greenbridge.co
